root_idea.summary: The root centers on fullness of flesh or fat, in contrast with leanness and emaciation; it also extends to fattening and ghee.
root_idea.development: The core idea of bodily or material fullness develops into becoming fat, causing fatness, possessing or supplying fatty provisions, and the noun سَمْنٌ for clarified butter. A regional divergent branch uses Form II for cooling.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Normalized from the Quranic Form IV imperfect يُسْمِنُ to the classical perfect citation form أَسْمَنَ.
The singular adjective سَمِينٌ is the appropriate citation form for the Quranic singular and plural adjective forms.

senses.definition: To fatten; to cause something to become fat or plump.
senses.usage_conditions: A causative transitive use. In the Quranic occurrence it is negated: the food does not produce fatness.

senses.definition: Fat, plump; having much flesh and fat.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic form occurs both as the singular سَمِينٍ and the plural سِمَانٍ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become fat or plump; to be in a condition of having much flesh and fat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form I intransitive usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of grain, to become full in the grain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension applied to wheat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To prepare, moisten, or stir food or bread with ghee.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form I transitive usage with food or bread as the object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To feed a person, people, or a group with ghee.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive provision-related use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To render someone or something fat or plump; to cause it to have much flesh and fat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II causative usage, distinct from the Quranic Form IV citation form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To furnish people with ghee as travelling provision or supplies.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A provision-related Form II use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cool something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A regional usage attributed to the dialects of al-Ṭāʾif and Yemen.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be fat or plump by nature.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive Form IV use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To possess, buy, or give a fat or plump thing; of a people, to come into the condition of having fat cattle; also, to buy ghee.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form is used for possession, acquisition, or transfer of fatty goods and for a community's condition with respect to fat cattle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a display or claim of abundance by hoarding wealth, boasting of goods not possessed, or claiming an unearned nobility.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or assumed-tropical extension.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To indulge in food and drink that cause fatness or plumpness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or assumed-tropical extension referring to fattening consumption.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To deem, reckon, or find a person or thing fat or plump.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object may be a person, an animal, flesh-meat, or another thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek or demand something fat or plump, including ghee.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A seeking or requesting use, including the expression for coming to request ghee.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Clarified butter; ghee. In the compound سَمْنُ الهَبِيدِ, decocted juice of colocynth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The ordinary noun denotes clarified butter from milk; the compound is a specialized lexical expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fatness or plumpness; the condition of having much flesh and fat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An abstract noun contrasted with leanness or emaciation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A particular herb with leaves, slender twigs, and a white flower.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plant name, distinct from the noun for ghee and the related noun for a fattening medicine.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A medicine used to fatten or render someone plump.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may refer specifically to a medicine used for fattening women.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sect or people associated with metempsychosis and related doctrines about the world's duration and the sources of knowledge.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized ethnoreligious designation, reported as an irregular relational noun from the name of an Indian town.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of land, fertile and productive, with good soil and few stones.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An assumed-tropical extension of the adjective for fatness, applied to land that strongly fosters plants or herbage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of speech, chaste, eloquent, or excellent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An assumed-tropical figurative use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A well-known bird, commonly identified with the quail.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used both as a singular and a plural; the singular may also occur as سُمَانَاةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A seller of ghee.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An occupational noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dyes or pigments used for decoration or embellishment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The name of a particular plant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plant name distinguished from the occupational noun سَمَّانٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A possessor of ghee.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A possessive nominal formation, parallel to nouns meaning a possessor of milk or dates.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Waist-wrappers; old and worn-out garments or pieces of cloth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized plural-like noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a people or party, having cattle that have become fat or plump.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized plural expression describing a community through the condition of its cattle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Food that causes fattening of the body.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine nominal form denotes a fattening property or effect.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Food made or prepared with ghee, or moistened and stirred with it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-participial adjective applied to food.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Form I becoming fat or plump.
Wheat becoming full in the grain.
Preparing or moistening food with ghee.
Seasoning bread with ghee is covered by preparing food with ghee.
Being fat or plump by nature.
Possessing, acquiring, giving fat goods, and the cattle-related community use.
Buying ghee is covered by the acquisition use.
The condition of having much ghee is covered by the possession use.
Figurative claims of abundance and indulgence in fattening food.
Finding or deeming something fat or plump.
Seeking or demanding ghee or something fat.
Specialized compound referring to decocted colocynth juice.
Abstract noun for fatness or plumpness.
Pointer-only cross-reference to the herb entry.
Fat or plump adjective, also directly Quran-attested.
Name of the quail or a related well-known bird.
Pointer-only cross-reference to the feminine of سَمِينٌ.
People whose cattle have become fat or plump.
Pointer-only cross-reference to the feminine of سَمِينٌ.
Food prepared or moistened with ghee.

cautions: The Quranic adjective is presented under the singular citation form سَمِينٌ, while the Quran also contains its plural form سِمَانٍ.
The regional cooling sense of سَمَّنَ is kept among broader Classical Arabic meanings and is not treated as a Quranic meaning.
